## How to read this list

`responsibilities` is verification-gated: only `{text: ..., verified: true}` is applicant experience, and `needs_verification` is excluded from every generated document (Master CV, tailored CV, cover letter, package text and email). A role title, a skill, a certificate, or the sector's normal practice is **not** evidence that a duty was performed — that is why these 28 lines are held.

| Action | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **CONFIRM** | The draft asserts nothing beyond the role you already record (supplied title, employer, work areas). Confirming it needs nothing more than your own attestation that the role is accurate. The wording must still be yours: no draft is paste-eligible. |
| **EDIT** | The draft's professional domain is named by your recorded role or by a verified competency/training, but the specific duty was never supplied. Keep it only if it is true, and author the wording yourself. |
| **DISCARD** | The draft's distinctive claim — a concrete activity, counterpart structure, or process — is named by no supplied fact and no verified item. It is a system inference about how the job is typically performed. Recommend rejecting unless you personally did exactly that. |

**Verbatim confirmation is not available for any line.** Each draft is measured against the same guard the release suite uses (`tests/test_cv_professional_quality.py`): a line may only be verified if it introduces no duty vocabulary and no named entity that you did not supply. Every one of the 28 drafts fails that guard as written, so a confirmed line must be your own sentence.

## What happens next (not performed by this tool)

1. Decide each line: CONFIRM (it is your experience), EDIT (keep the substance in your own words), or DISCARD (reject the inference).
2. `profile.yaml` changes only when you make them. A confirmed line becomes applicant experience only when you move `{text: <your wording>, verified: true}` into that role's `responsibilities`; discarded lines can be deleted from `needs_verification` in the same edit.
3. Check any candidate wording before you record it: `python tools/export_responsibility_review.py --verify-wording "your wording"` (read-only).
4. Re-run the suite: `python -m pytest -q`.

_This list is a presentation of the canonical record. It does not modify `profile.yaml`, it does not merge or release anything, and it does not apply a decision on your behalf._
